notes:
Concrete notes from calls and POC. Fragments + quotes.
- Company: mid-market analytics SaaS, heavy EU user base (Germany/France/Netherlands).
- Primary ask: start on Redwood hosted API for rapid POC, then evaluate Dedicated for predictable latency & costs once model mix stabilizes.
- "Prefer EU-only hosting for production; can accept multi-region if tokens never leave EU jurisdiction" — Head of Security (Anna Muller).
- Performance targets: 95th pct latency < 200ms for short chat turn (<=512 tokens), sustained peak throughput 200-250 TPS for background reranking; daytime burst to 400 TPS for onboarding events.
- Cost sensitivity: wants per-token cost to be within 20% of current vendor baseline for embeddings and gen, otherwise will require committed capacity.
- Routing: interested in smart-routing rules — eu-primary, fallback to mru (eu/dedicated) before us-east; must quantify added RTT when failing over.
- POC technical notes: SE ran hosted API against sample dataset (50k docs) using embeddings+approx nearest neighbor rerank. Observed: eu-west host avg latency 90-130ms for 64-dim embeddings call, generation median 85ms (short prompts), 95th ~120ms. When simulating us-east fallback RTT adds ~80-120ms.
- Dedicated conversation: discussed GPU pool sizing (2x A10-equivalent) to hit 250 TPS with batching and KV cache. SE recommended quantized model variant to reduce cost by ~25% vs fp16.
- Security & compliance: request for SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence (they have their own SOC2 in progress), mandatory SSO via SAML, KMS integration for key wrapping.
- Data residency specifics: legal wants contract language ensuring EU data stays in EU for both at-rest and in-transit processing for production traffic; tolerates logs/telemetry export to Redwood control plane in US only if pseudonymized and subject to EU SCCs.
- Blocker note from Legal: "Cannot sign until we have explicit EU-residency SLA and right-to-audit clause."
- Business note: If Dedicated bid returns ARR estimate within their budget (100k-250k) and residency clause satisfied, probability to move to procurement in April.
- Misc: asked for a brief runbook for migration from hosted -> dedicated with expected downtime and rollback steps. SE to produce by 2026-03-18.
